prompt: Which of these break a rule of hooks? Choose every one.
hint: Top level, and only from components or hooks.

choices.text: `useState` inside an `if`
choices.why: Breaks rule one.

choices.text: `useEffect` after an early `return`
choices.why: Breaks rule one.

choices.text: `useState` called from a click handler
choices.why: Breaks rule two.

choices.text: A custom hook `useWeek` that calls `useState`
choices.why: Allowed: a hook may call hooks.

prompt: Why may a function named `useWeekLogger` call `useEffect`, when an ordinary helper may not?
hint: When is a custom hook called?

choices.text: It is called during a render, like a component
choices.why: Right. The name tells the linter and the reader that it will be.

choices.text: React reads the `use` prefix at run time and switches modes
choices.why: React never reads the name; the prefix is for tools and people.

choices.text: Hooks are allowed anywhere in TypeScript files
choices.why: The rule has nothing to do with the language.

choices.text: Because it is exported
choices.why: Exporting changes nothing.

prompt: How does React know which `useState` call is `monday`?

choices.text: By the name of the variable it is assigned to
choices.why: The name never reaches React; destructuring happens after the call returns.

choices.text: By the type of its initial value
choices.why: Several slots hold strings; the type cannot tell them apart.

choices.text: By its position in the order of calls
choices.why: Right. The first call gets slot one, every render.

choices.text: By a hidden key the compiler adds
choices.why: No key is added; order is the whole mechanism.

prompt: Why did React choose order over a key per hook, such as `useState('open', false)`?
hint: Think of two custom hooks inside one component.

choices.text: Strings are slow to compare
choices.why: Speed was not the argument.

choices.text: Two hooks could pick the same key
choices.why: Right. Order cannot collide, because each component's list is its own.

choices.text: TypeScript cannot type a string key
choices.why: It can; the problem is two hooks using the same string.

choices.text: Keys are reserved for lists
choices.why: That is a different `key`, for elements.

prompt: With the early `return` above the title effect, how many hooks did `App` call on its first render?
Why did the app with the early `return` disappear completely, rather than show the loading line?
hint: What happens to the tree when rendering throws?

choices.text: The loading line was drawn and then hidden by CSS
choices.why: No CSS was involved; the tree was removed.

choices.text: An uncaught render error
choices.why: Right. Lesson 12 shows how to catch it.

choices.text: The fetch failed
choices.why: The fetch succeeded; the render after it threw.

choices.text: Vite's overlay covered it
choices.why: The overlay is for compile errors; this one happened at run time.

prompt: What did the type check say about the early `return` above two effects?

choices.text: An error at the `return`
choices.why: It passed.

choices.text: No errors
choices.why: Right. The rules of hooks are not types; the linter checks them.

choices.text: A warning that the effect is unreachable
choices.why: TypeScript cannot know the effect is unreachable on some renders.

choices.text: It refused to run while the dev server was up
choices.why: They run side by side.

prompt: After "Show minutes left", an empty week and back, the summary said "80 of 195". What happened to `showLeft`?
hint: In the empty week the component called no hooks.

choices.text: It was reset to its initial value
choices.why: Right. React dropped the only slot and later made a fresh one.

choices.text: It was kept, and the button lied about it
choices.why: The button and the line agreed: both showed `false`.

choices.text: It moved to `WeekNav`'s slot
choices.why: Each component has its own list.

choices.text: It became `undefined` and React printed an error
choices.why: Nothing was printed; that is why this version is worse.

prompt: Why did the one-hook `WeekSummary` lose its state silently while `App` crashed?

choices.text: `WeekSummary` is not inside strict mode
choices.why: Everything is inside strict mode in this app.

choices.text: A component with no slots looks new, so there was no mismatch to detect
choices.why: Right. With hooks on both sides of the `return`, it would have crashed too.

choices.text: React checks hook order only in `App`
choices.why: React checks every component the same way.

choices.text: `useState` is safe after a return; `useEffect` is not
choices.why: Both are hooks and follow the same rule.

prompt: With 80 of 195 minutes done, how many minutes did "Show minutes left" display?
Which rule found the hook after the early `return`?

choices.text: `exhaustive-deps`
choices.why: That one reads dependency arrays.

choices.text: `only-export-components`
choices.why: That one is about fast refresh and exports.

choices.text: TypeScript's `strict` mode
choices.why: TypeScript passed.

choices.text: `rules-of-hooks`
choices.why: Right.

prompt: `const [a, setA] = ok ? useState(1) : [1, () => {}]` is one line. Why does the linter still refuse it?

choices.text: The hook is called on one side of a condition only
choices.why: Right. It pointed at both halves of the expression.

choices.text: Arrays cannot replace a hook's return value
choices.why: Type-wise they can; the rule is about order.

choices.text: Ternaries are forbidden in components
choices.why: Ternaries are everywhere in JSX.

choices.text: The line is too long for the formatter
choices.why: That is a formatter's concern, not a linter rule.

prompt: The template runs Oxlint with the command `npm run ___`.
After "Next week", the interval with `[]` still logged 19 October. Why?

choices.text: `setInterval` copies the values it is given once, when it starts
choices.why: It received no arguments; the function read a captured variable.

choices.text: The click did not change `monday`
choices.why: The screen showed the new week.

choices.text: It closed over the first render's `monday`
choices.why: Right, and the empty array never let the effect run again.

choices.text: Strict mode keeps a copy of the old state
choices.why: Strict mode keeps no copies.

prompt: What did adding `monday` to the interval's array change?

choices.text: Nothing visible, since the interval had been correct all along
choices.why: The log changed from 19 to 26 October.

choices.text: The old interval was cleared and a new one started
choices.why: Right. The new one closed over the new week.

choices.text: The interval ran twice as often
choices.why: One interval at a time.

choices.text: The interval read `monday` from the DOM
choices.why: It reads the variable it captured.

prompt: The keyboard effect keeps `[]` and is not stale. What makes it safe?

choices.text: Keyboard events are always fresh
choices.why: The event is fresh; a captured variable would not be.

choices.text: `window` listeners are re-created on every render
choices.why: With `[]` it is created once.

choices.text: It is inside `App`, which never re-renders
choices.why: `App` re-renders on every state change.

choices.text: It uses the updater form, so React hands it the latest week
choices.why: Right. Re-running the effect would add listeners for nothing.

prompt: A colleague writes `if (!user) return null` at the top of a component that has three hooks below. What do you suggest?
hint: The order fix from the section.

choices.text: Move the hooks above the `return`
choices.why: Right: every hook first, then every return.

choices.text: Wrap each hook in `if (user)`
choices.why: That breaks the same rule three times.

choices.text: Turn off `rules-of-hooks` for this file
choices.why: The rule is right; the code is wrong.

choices.text: Leave it: it works while `user` exists
choices.why: It breaks the day `user` changes between renders.

prompt: A component's effect subscribes to a chat room named by a prop, with `[]`. The prop changes from `general` to `random`. What does the user see?
hint: The subscription was made by the first render.

choices.text: Messages from `random`, because the prop changed
choices.why: The effect never ran again to subscribe to it.

choices.text: No messages, because the effect errors
choices.why: Nothing errors; it is silent.

choices.text: The old room's messages under the new name
choices.why: Right. The heading renders from the prop; the subscription is stale.

choices.text: Both rooms, merged
choices.why: Only one subscription was ever made.
